proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating oxyanion Li-ion conductor. Its P-O bonding is highly oxidation-resistant, so it should stay stable against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V. It is also chemically compatible with the sulfide Li6PS5Cl, so it can act as a buffer layer that limits interfacial decomposition and space-charge formation.

Li3PO4 failed because its contact with the sulfide electrolyte was reducing and produced oxidized S and P species (P2O5, SO2, SCl4) with a penalty of 0.337 eV/atom. LiF is a wide-gap, highly oxidation-resistant Li-ion insulator. Its F- anion is hard to oxidize and forms very stable Li-F bonds, so it should be less prone to redox with both LiCoO2 at 4.0 V and Li6PS5Cl. It is a different chemical family from the prior oxyanion coating, so it is an exploratory test of the halide route.
